articles.title: Meet 'America': Trump’s AI chatbot changes answers after challenging his claims
articles.description: Donald Trump has launched “America”, an AI chatbot designed as a digital portal for US government information. But its responses appear to be changing. The chatbot initially challenged several of Trump’s claims, including on the 2020 election and inflation, providing evidence and links. More recently, it has refused to answer some of the same questions. Other responses still contradict Trump, while some echo his views. Vedika Bahl tests the chatbot, and its varying answers in Truth or Fake.

articles.title: Israel PM says pilot of rerouted flight tried to crash plane
articles.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday that the pilot of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight had tried to crash the plane and kill its passengers, after the aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Passengers gave a similar account of the incident on board, describing a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted, losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

articles.title: Russia ramps up disinformation attacks on French media ahead of 2027 Presidential race
articles.description: Pro-Russian influence operations have caused a surge of 850% in fake news stories mimicking real media brands, according to a report published this week by disinformation specialist, NewsGuard. Out of the 15 most imitated news outlets, eight are French – including FRANCE 24.

articles.title: Why is the US withdrawing its troops from Iraq?
articles.description: A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight jihadists concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country's leaders, but which some fear will embolden pro-Iran armed factions. France 24's Angela Diffley takes a look at the security challenges facing the country and why the US has chosen this moment to take its troops out.

related.title: US forces leave Iraq, raising fears of Iran-backed militias amid power vacuum

articles.title: Ex-TV anchor crowned as king in Uganda after succession fight

Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma succeeded King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, whose death ​last month from ‌cancer at age 34 triggered a feud, with his mother saying a previously undisclosed son was entitled to ⁠the throne.

articles.title: Mixed reactions in Iraq on final day of US-led coalition withdrawal
articles.description: The US military announced on Wednesday that it has completed the withdrawal of all American troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission to fight the Islamic State group. The last US troops left an air base in northern Iraq under a deal between Baghdad and Washington.

articles.title: Medicine prices soar in Iran as US blockade and sanctions hit hard

articles.title: Was Netanyahu warned of October 7 Hamas attacks?

articles.title: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri named Morocco's first woman PM
articles.description: The king of Morocco on Tuesday named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri the country's first woman prime minister after her centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) party won last week's parliamentary elections. El Mansouri joined the PAM in 2008 and was also the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh, winning the office in 2009 before losing it six years later, then retaking it again in 2021.

articles.title: Ethiopia's last Jews dream of visa for Israel
articles.description: Ethiopia has one of the oldest Jewish communities in the world, rumoured to be the descendants of the Queen of Sheba and King Solomon in 950 BC. From the 1970s to 1990s, this community known as Beta Israel was persecuted under the Communist regime, and Israel evacuated more than 20,000 Ethiopian Jews in dramatic airlifts known as Operation Solomon and Operation Moses. But a few thousand were left behind.

articles.title: Attention turns to economy on final day of Macron’s visit to Spain

articles.title: 'Hard to see Man City getting anything other than the book thrown at them', expert says
articles.description: Manchester City enjoyed a meteoric rise from mid-table mediocrity to Premier League domination, but their golden era could be forever tarnished after they were found guilty of scores of financial rule breaches. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with James Reade, Professor of Economics at the University of Reading. He says that it's unlikely that the club will see any leniency from football authorities: "it's hard to see it getting anything other than the book thrown at them".

articles.title: Live: Several people killed as Russia launches new round of strikes on Kyiv
articles.description: At least three people, including a child, have died after Russia launched another round of strikes on Kyiv and its surrounding regions overnight to Wednesday, officials said. Several people were also wounded in the attacks. In Poland, two airports, in Lublin and Rzeszow, were briefly shut over “military aviation activity” during Russian attacks on Ukraine. articles.title: Clashes between French teens, police as school blockades intensify
articles.description: French teenagers on Tuesday set fire to rubbish bins and threw projectiles at police who responded with batons and tear gas, with hundreds detained across the country over the blockades and protests demanding better conditions at schools. Since last week, students have staged protests outside hundreds of schools over grievances including timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers as well as overheated classrooms during this year's heatwaves. articles.title: Vol de FlyDubai vers Tel-Aviv dérouté : Benyamin Nétanyahou salue le courage du pilote indien attaqué par son copilote

articles.title: Affaire Epstein : la diplomatie norvégienne sur le gril

articles.title: Routes détruites, logements inondés… L'équivalent de deux mois de pluie tombent en quelques heures dans le Gard

articles.title: Crash du Dubaï-Tel Aviv évité : comment la sécurité est-elle assurée à bord d'un avion ?

Retour sur les faits et leurs zones d'ombre, et tour d'horizon des procédures en vigueur.
